about: Unicode text -> Shree-Lipi 7 Devanagari (SHREE-DEV7-xxxx, S<dddd>892.TTF; Hindi and Marathi, and Sanskrit typed in a DEV7 font - NOT the SHREE-SAN7 fonts, see counts.sanskritCheck) bytes, answered by Shree's own composers S8DevU64.dll and S8Dev764.dll for the same keystroke. bytes = the 7 composer's raw output, one hex byte per glyph code. kind: vendor-key = a key of one of the 39 shipped .DEV keyboards (layers 0, Ctrl+Space, Ctrl+Shift+1; source names the keyboard, key and the internal codes the key holds); canonical = probe in Shree's typing order (i-sign struck first, reph struck after base+sign); canonical:ligature-code = the conjunct or nukta letter typed with its own code (क्ष ज्ञ श्र त्र त्त क़ ख़ ...), preferred; canonical:pending-link = sequence ending in a Link, the composer answers the half form it is waiting with; link+ya / ya-sign code D5 / reph-then-anusvara / anusvara-then-reph = other accepted orders; alt:* = the composer answer for a non-canonical typing order or a visibly different form (kept, not used as truth); quirk:* = the Unicode composer wrote something other than the code sequence means (misaligned), or the 7 composer silently dropped a code the Unicode composer wrote (ॢ ॣ ॡ, nukta typed as D9, a trailing Link after the ra-sign), or wrote a byte that does not draw the character (B3 for ”, 9D for the EE nukta) (kept for evidence, not used). Unicode keys are exactly what the Unicode composer wrote: क़ ख़ ग़ ज़ ड़ ढ़ फ़ य़ ऩ ऱ ऴ typed with their own codes come back precomposed (U+0958-U+095F, U+0929, U+0931, U+0934) with the nukta drawn before the letter (B5/8B) or as a ligature (ख़ 98); the nukta key (code EE, Ctrl+Space 3 on most keyboards) comes back from the Unicode composer as U+093C (a consonant + EE decomposed, C + U+093C), but the 7 composer has no nukta for it - it writes 9D, a short piece of headline (8F, the ÷ glyph, before a Link) - so every EE pair is quirk:* and a decomposed C + U+093C has no truth: DEV7 draws a nukta only for the letters that have their own code (normalise to the precomposed letter first). Characters the DEV7 fonts cannot draw come back as a stand-in and are quirk:* too: ₹ as 3C (no glyph at 3C in any installed DEV7 or DEV 4/5/6 font), ऌ as 2A (the * glyph), ॆ as 90 (an empty glyph, so ऎ ऒ ऄ ॊ lose the mark); ॢ ॣ ॡ ॑ ᳚ ॰ ॺ ॥ get no byte at all. The family-differing bytes (91 92 B3 B6, see family-diff-456-vs-7.json) never occur in an answer except B3 for ” (quirk); ङ्क ङ्ख ङ्म come back as ङ + halant B2 + letter, not as the 4/5/6 ligatures 91 92 B6, so every answer also draws the same in a SHREE-DEV-0700/4914 (4/5/6) font except the one B3. The composer's rules with examples: dev7-patterns.txt.

sanskritCheck.note: S8SanU64/S8San764 on the same probe keyboards: the Unicode answers are identical, the bytes differ almost everywhere - SHREE-SAN7-0960/0962/0964 fonts use an encoding of their own (rendered check: these bytes draw garbage in a SAN7 font, the Sanskrit composer's bytes draw the right text). This file is NOT ground truth for SHREE-SAN7 fonts; see san7-groundtruth.json.
